history.dynasty: Kureekad Swaroopam (local rulers); later the royal family of Cochin, whose tutelary deity Poornathrayeesa was
history.period: Traditionally Dwapara Yuga; historical records mention installation/reinstallation in 947 AD; present idol recast 1270 AD; current structures rebuilt 1921–1932 after a 1920 fire
history.summary: Sree Poornathrayeesa Temple at Thrippunithura was the foremost of the eight royal temples of the erstwhile Kingdom of Cochin, and Poornathrayeesa — 'God of the Three Vedas' — was the tutelary deity of the Cochin royal family. Legend says Lord Vishnu gifted the idol to Arjuna, who brought it here in his chariot after restoring the ten children of a Brahmin (the Santhanagopalam episode of the Bhagavatha); this is why the sanctum is shaped like a chariot and the deity is worshipped as Santhanagopala Murthy, the saviour of infants. The same legend explains the unique south-facing Ganesha: Arjuna is said to have nudged the already-seated Ganapati aside to install Vishnu's idol, and the Poornathrayeesa temple is the only temple where Ganesha faces south. Historical records mention an installation in 947 AD; the present idol was recast in 1270 AD and the temple structures were built in stages from 952 to 1849 AD. A massive fire in 1920 destroyed everything except the sanctum and the idol; the temple was rebuilt in concrete (replacing the original wood) by architect Sri Eachara Warrier, with the fourth Dhwaja Stambham installed in 1932. The Cochin royal family controlled the temple until it passed to the Cochin Devaswom Board.

name: Sree Poornathrayeesa Temple
town_description: Thrippunithura (Tripunithura) is the historic former capital of the Kingdom of Cochin, now a suburb of Kochi in Ernakulam district, Kerala. Known for the Hill Palace (the former royal palace, now a museum), its classical music and dance traditions, and a dense cluster of ancient temples, it was the seat of the Cochin royal family whose national deity was Sree Poornathrayeesa.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (approx. 33 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Thrippunithura station is within the town; Ernakulam Junction (approx. 8 km), well connected across India.
travel.road: In the heart of Thrippunithura (Kottakakom, PIN 682301); easily reached by city buses, autos and taxis from Kochi/Ernakulam.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Vrischikotsavam (November–December) is the grandest time to visit, with elephant processions and cultural programmes.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning approx. 4:00 AM to 11:15 AM; evening approx. 4:00 PM to 8:15 PM (verify — closing times vary by source between 8:00 PM and 8:30 PM). No entry fee; traditional modest dress advised; mobile phones restricted inside.
